details.description:
Buck Hall Recreation Area offers a premier location to enjoy the outdoors. It is situated along the Intracoastal Waterway and provides great access to Cape Romain National Wildlife Refuge, 65,000 acres of marsh, tidal creeks and beaches; and Bulls Bay, the coast's best shrimp baiting area. The recreation area boasts a large picnic area and multiple campsites for tent and RV camping. Electricity and water hookups are available. Each site is equipped with a table, lantern post and campfire ring with grill.
Accessible flush toilets, showers and drinking water are provided. The picnic area is equipped with tables, grills, an accessible walkway and fish cleaning station. A lighted parking area and boat ramp are on-site.

properties.name: WOODALL SHOALS CHATTOOGA RIVER ACCESS
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description:
From this location, boaters and river visitors can access Section IV of the Chattooga Wild and Scenic River.  Boaters can pick-up a permit at the parking lot before putting-in here.  All visitors recreating at Woodall Shoals should maintain caution when near the water: the rapids on the river here and downstream are beautiful to approach and view, but they are also extremely powerful and unpredictable which poses a significant risk to all river users.  All boaters are required to wear helmets and life jackets, and swimming/wading above rapids is dangerous and strongly discouraged.
The geologic formations along the bank are also fun to play on and create micro-ecosystems for a variety of biological life, and these rocks are frequently submerged during high-water and are very smooth and slippery as a result of weathering.  Exploration is encouraged, but be careful when traversing the rocks and keep a close eye on children playing here.

details.description:
Sedalia Seasonal Camp is part of the Enoree Ranger District of the Francis Marion Sumter National Forest, managed by the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Forest Service. This camp offers a rustic setting ideal for camping, canoeing, or hiking  Palmetto Trail.  The front campground is open year round.  The back loop is open seasonally, only April, then again September through December.   There is a 2 week stay limit throughout the entire campground, year-round.  The surrounding forest environment sustains abundant wildlife populations, resulting in some of the most desirable hunting.
 There are supply stores in the vicinity, on SC 72 and SC 215.
 There are other recreation opportunities in the area.  Fishing is popular at the Johns Creek Lakes complex.  You can hike south from this camp for 38 miles of the Enoree Passage of the
Palmetto Trail.  Or down in Newberry County, there is a Enoree OHV Trail which allows riders of 50" or smaller ATV's and motorbikes to ride well maintained trails.

properties.name: WOODS FERRY BOAT RAMP
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: The Broad River flows along the eastern side of the Enoree District for approximately 32 miles. Called the Broad River since 1745, it once was a boundary between the Cherokee and Catawba Indian tribes. The river runs through a millrace at Lockhart leaving the riverbed virtually dry for more than a mile. The best points to get onto the river are five miles down river at the Broad River boat ramp or Woods Ferry Recreation area. The 16.6 mile float to Neal Shoals Dam is primarily flat-water with a few riffles. There is a small inlet to the river on the east bank where you can portage .4 miles around the dam. Once around the dam, the river passes under Hwy. 72/121 (no access). The Sandy River flows into the Broad from the east, and there is an access point just around the bend of the confluence. South of the Sandy River is the liveliest part of the trip. Riffles and ledges are present but the paddling is not difficult. The next landmark is Shelton Island; stay to the right channel. Henderson Island is next and a nice place to take a break. Take the left channel. As you travel under the Hwy. 34 bridge, you leave the forest. The Woods Ferry Boat Ramp is one of six boat ramps in the Enoree Ranger District management area along the Broad River. From Woods Ferry to the Neal Shoals Dam, small boats with motors may be used. Canoes and flat-bottom boats less than 14 feet long are recommended for the remainder of the river.
details.feeDescription: No fees are required for this site
details.hours: Day use only: open sunrise to sunset
details.directions: From Hwy. 72 and Leeds Rd., drive north 1.8 miles. Turn left onto County Rd. 49 drive .10 miles. Cross railroad tracks and drive north 3.4 miles. Take left on Park Rd. Drive 3.6 miles to end of paved road. From Hwy. 9 and County 49, drive south 5.6 miles. Turn right on Park Rd. and drive 3.6 miles to end of paved road. FS road 304 to Neal Shoals Dam and Canoe access-portage only

properties.name: ROSE HILL
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: While floating the 24 mile stretch of the Tyger River, visitors will find bottomland forests and small marshy areas. The river ranges from two to six feet deep and 40 to 70 feet wide. Paddlers may encounter a variety of water levels so experiences depend on the time of year and the amount of rainfall. Early spring brings heavy rains that cause the river to swell, making it unsafe to paddle. In late spring, river conditions provide fast-moving flatwater for experienced paddlers to enjoy. The summer months, coupled with a lack of rain, turn the river into a small creek that makes boating impossible. In the fall, the rains start again, and river conditions provide fast-moving, flat water. Floaters have excellent opportunities to view many wildlife species and  abundant plant life or to fish  for catfish, bream, and redeye bass. The Rose Hill boat ramp is one of five boat ramps in the Enoree Ranger District management area along the Tyger River Canoe Trail. Canoes and flat-bottom boats less than 14 feet long are recommended.

details.hours: Day use only: open sunrise to sunset

details.description:
Indian Creek Rifle Range is part of the Francis Marion Sumter National Forest, and is located on the Enoree Ranger District.  It is managed by the Forest Service, under the U.S. Department of Agriculture.
This year round rifle range has been designed with the firearm and hunting enthusiast in mind.  This rifle range has right and left shooting benches and 1 that is wheelchair accessible.  It has backstops up close to accommodate pistol shooters and one at 100 yards to accommodate all other users.
All firearms must meet SC firearm regulations and safety standards. Ranges are pack it in, pack it out. Shooters are responsible for own cleanup of all bullet casings, target and target holder, litter-trash. This includes all pieces of stationary, biodegradable skeet being used as a target. Properly dispose of all litter.
Nearby attractions include Molly's Rock Picnic Area with a 1 mile loop trail, picnic pavilion and pond with a pier.  The Enoree Ranger Station is .1 miles away.

$50 per person per year

If you miss your turn drive north and at the top of the hill is the Enoree Ranger District Office where you can safely turn around and go back. Use caution on this road. details.description: While floating the 24 mile stretch of the Tyger River, visitors will find bottomland forests and small marshy areas. The river ranges from two to six feet deep and 40 to 70 feet wide. Paddlers may encounter a variety of water levels so experiences depend on the time of year and the amount of rainfall. Early spring brings heavy rains that cause the river to swell, making it unsafe to paddle. In late spring, river conditions provide fast-moving flatwater for experienced paddlers to enjoy. The summer months, coupled with a lack of rain, turn the river into a small creek that makes boating impossible. In the fall, the rains start again, and river conditions provide fast-moving, flat water. Floaters have excellent opportunities to view many wildlife species and  abundant plant life or to fish  for catfish, bream, and redeye bass. The Beattys Bridge boat ramp is one of five boat ramps in the Enoree Ranger District management area along the Tyger River Canoe Trail. Canoes and flat-bottom boats less than 14 feet long are recommended.

Sewee Center's schedule of events changes monthly... For the latest line-up of free events and classes, visit the Event Calendar at Cape Romain National Wildlife Refuge | Events | U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service (fws.gov).

Views of bluffs covered with live oak and palmetto trees give way to vistas of open water and red cedar-covered dredge islands of the Intracoastal Waterway.  The creek provides access to Cape Romain National Wildlife Refuge, its barrier islands and great shore birding opportunities. Paddlers can spot a rich variety of wildlife such as dolphins, blue herons, fiddler crabs, pelicans and oystercatchers. The area also serves as a trailhead for the Awendaw Passage of the Palmetto Trail.

It is a picture of a land in recovery.
The boardwalk overlooks a prehistoric shell mound and offers five interpretive stops in addition to breathtaking views of the salt marsh, tidal creek and the Intracoastal Waterway.

properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description: The Broad River flows along the eastern side of the Enoree District for approximately 32 miles. Called the Broad River since 1745, it once was a boundary between the Cherokee and Catawba Indian tribes. The river runs through a millrace at Lockhart leaving the riverbed virtually dry for more than a mile. The best points to get onto the river are five miles down river at the Broad River boat ramp or Woods Ferry Recreation area. The 16.6 mile float to Neal Shoals Dam is primarily flat-water with a few riffles. There is a small inlet to the river on the east bank where you can portage .4 miles around the dam. Once around the dam, the river passes under Hwy. 72/121 (no access). The Sandy River flows into the Broad from the east, and there is an access point just around the bend of the confluence. South of the Sandy River is the liveliest part of the trip. Riffles and ledges are present but the paddling is not difficult. The next landmark is Shelton Island; stay to the right channel. Henderson Island is next and a nice place to take a break. Take the left channel. As you travel under the Hwy. 34 bridge, you leave the forest. The Broad River Boat Ramp is one of six boat ramps in the Enoree Ranger District management area along the Broad River. From Woods Ferry to the Neal Shoals Dam, small boats with motors may be used. Canoes and flat-bottom boats less than 14 feet long are recommended for the remainder of the river.

The surrounding forest environment sustains abundant wildlife populations resulting in some of the most  desirable hunting in the state.  The campground is open seasonally for hunting, only April for turkey season, then again September through December for deer season.  The surrounding forest environment sustains abundant wildlife populations, resulting in some of the most desirable hunting. properties.name: BRICK HOUSE
properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description:
Brick House Campground is part of the Enoree Ranger District of the Francis Marion Sumter National Forest, managed by the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Forest Service.
This campground offers a primitive setting for camping, while enjoying the natural surroundings.
The surrounding forest environment sustains abundant wildlife populations, resulting in some of the most desirable hunting areas in the state. Other recreational opportunities in the area include hiking the Enoree Passage of the Palmetto Trail, horse riding on the 31-mile Buncombe Horse Trail, riding an OHV on the 24 miles of Enoree OHV Trail, wildlife viewing, photography, biking, and other outdoor activities.  Please note, you will need to bring your own bike, ATV (less than 50"), dirt bike or horse to enjoy the aforementioned trails.

details.description: The Enoree Off Highway Vehicle (OHV) Trail travels along rolling piedmont hills and through pine forests. The trail is only managed for all-terrain vehicles (ATVs) and dirt or dual sports bikes. Jeeps, Hummers and other 4 x 4 vehicles are not allowed on trails. properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description:
Fairforest Rifle Range is part of the Francis Marion Sumter National Forest, and is located on the Enoree Ranger District.  It is managed by the Forest Service, under the U.S. Department of Agriculture.
This year round rifle range has been designed with the firearm and hunting enthusiast in mind.  This rifle range has right and left shooting benches and 1 that is wheelchair accessible.  It has backstops up close to accommodate pistol shooters and one at 100 yards to accommodate all other users.
All firearms must meet SC firearm regulations and safety standards. Ranges are pack it in, pack it out. Shooters are responsible for own cleanup of all bullet casings, target and target holder, litter-trash. This includes all pieces of stationary, biodegradable skeet being used as a target. Properly dispose of all litter.
Nearby attractions include Sedalia Campground and the Palmetto Trail. The Enoree Ranger Station is 25 miles away.

details.description: This picnic area features a stone and timber picnic shelter built in the 1930s by the Civilian Conservation Corps and a curving boardwalk winding through the cool streamside forest past picnic spots and a fishing pier.  Hikers can access the East Fork Trail leading into the Ellicott Rock Wilderness from the picnic area.  Visitors here can also access the adjacent Walhalla State Fish Hatchery where South Carolina Department of Natural Resources raises brown and rainbow trout to stock local watersheds.  Site amenities include picnic tables, small fire pits/grills, and vault toilet facilities.

details.description:
Buck Hall Recreation Area offers a premier location to enjoy the outdoors. It is situated along the Intracoastal Waterway and provides great access to Cape Romain National Wildlife Refuge, 65,000 acres of marsh, tidal creeks and beaches; and Bulls Bay, the coast's best shrimp baiting area. The recreation area boasts a large picnic area and multiple campsites for tent and RV camping. Electricity and water hookups are available. Each site is equipped with a table, lantern post and campfire ring with grill.
Accessible flush toilets, showers and drinking water are provided. The picnic area is equipped with tables, grills, an accessible walkway and fish cleaning station. A lighted parking area and boat ramp are on-site.

properties.publicUse: USFS recreation site; verify current season, fees, access and closures.

details.description:
Collins Creek Seasonal Camp is part of the Enoree Ranger
District of the Francis Marion Sumter National Forest, managed by the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Forest Service.
This site is opened seasonally in April for Turkey hunting
season. Then opened again from September through
December for Deer hunting season. It is closed in the summer and early spring.
This camp offers a rustic setting, ideal for camping while
enjoying the opportunities to hunt the area. The surrounding forest environment sustains abundant wildlife populations,
resulting in some of the most desirable hunting areas in the state.
There are other recreation opportunities nearby. Enjoy a mile long hike on the Jew's Harp Spring Trail; access is located across from the shower building. This trail will take you to see the original spring house. Brazzlemens Bridge Ramp, located 5.8 miles south of the campground, is a great place to launch a boat and go fishing.
